newsitem.title: USA: Oakmont Steel resumes production with new credit.
newsitem.headline: Oakmont Steel resumes production with new credit.

text.p: The United Steelworkers of America said Thursday Oakmont Steel Corp, doing business as Edgewater Steel, has resumed production of railroad wheels and steel rings after negotiating new terms with its major secured creditor, CIT Group Holdings.
CIT is 80 percent owned by Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and 20 percent by Chase Manhattan Corp.
Oakmont Steel is developing a long-term business plan, and is actively seeking investors to provide working capital, the union said.
Steelworkers Local 1246 President Carl Runski, who also sits on Oakmont Steel's board, said, "We've gone from a near shutdown at the end of February to a start-up under new management in March."
Anthony Rinaldi, an Oakmont Steel director and mill manager, replaced former President James Sumner February 28, the union said.

Runski said Oakmont Steel is working closely with current customers, such as General Motors Corp, a major purchaser of forged railroad wheels, and Caterpillar Inc and SKF Corp, buyers of steel rings, to meet current production goals. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
